The primary function of games is to educate and entertain. They involve skill, knowledge, and chance. They often contain rules and objectives that require strategy and planning to succeed. Aside from the educational benefit, games are often fun and entertaining. Those who enjoy playing these games are rewarded with positive feedback and the chance to win prizes. This is because there is no direct competition in these games. Moreover, the games are educational and provide a way to express emotions and solve problems.

Games are a great way to entertain and educate. Most of them are interactive and encourage people to make modifications. Some of these modifications may involve coding and graphics, but the main objective is to improve the game’s quality. There are many types of games, including board games, card games, and guessing games. These games are fun and can help develop critical and practical thinking skills. A game can also be educational. It can enhance a person’s social skills, improve their memory, or provide a sense of accomplishment.

A game has different key elements, and all of them are important. The rules and tools of a game are important. The players’ actions influence the outcome of the game. The key elements of a game define the context and the core mechanics of a particular game. A successful work will be unique, while a poor one will not be. A good example of this is a chess piece that is a clone of another game.

What is Gambling and How to Keep Your Money Safe

GAMBLING is an international commercial activity. The total amount wagered on legal games of chance, such as lottery tickets, was $335 billion in 2009. Some forms of gambling involve materials that have value. For example, a marbles player may bet on the outcome of a game. Another example is a Magic: The Gathering player who stakes his collectible game pieces. The odds of winning depend on luck. This article will describe some types of gambling and how to keep your money safe.

In the United Kingdom, the Gambling Commission regulates these activities. While there is no specific definition for gambling, the term is often used to describe any wagering activity. This may include collecting game pieces or playing marbles. In both cases, the player risks losing their money. Many types of gambling involve risk and reward.

RC) Nepal is the implementing partner agency of the NPP Program in Nepal.

NPP-NSC consists of members from the government (Joint Secretary, Disaster and Conflict Management Division, Ministry of Home Affairs) as the Chair of the committee and Co-chairs representing the Local Government/Municipal Association, the Private Sector (FNCCI), Academia (Tribhuvan University), and key government and civil society organizations representatives. The Under Secretary, Disaster Study Risk Reduction and Recovery Section, MOHA, serves as Ex-Officio member secretary of NPP and the implementing Agency (NDRC Nepal) / APP Partner is the de-facto member of the NPP – NSC.

Key Impacts of APP II NPP: 2017 – 2023

1. Private Sector Engagement and Strengthening Resilience Business:
Introduction of Business Continuity Management and Plan (BCM/P) Training to the private sector; promoted and
facilitated their engagement in DRR/M as well as developed trained human resources at the national level for BCM
in Nepal.
2. Strengthening DRRM localization:
The multifaceted partnership approach contributed to improving risk governance at the local levels through resource
leveraging in enhancing local governments’ DRRM capacity (LDCRP (Local Disaster and Climate Resilience Plan)/LSAR
(Light Search and Rescue Material)/DRRM Knowledge Management) and integration of GESI in the local level DRRM planning.
3. Upscaling Protection against Lightning (PaL):
Partnership with Academia contributed to strengthening national government policy and capacity on PaL initiatives,
through the development of the PaL & EFSS Training Manual, PaL Approach Paper, and PaL/EFSS training).
4. Empowering and promoting Local Humanitarian Organizations:
Successfully established Networking of Local Humanitarian Organizations (NDRNet) representing LHOs from the grassroots. The NDRNet has been playing a crucial role in the coordination, assessment, and information management of disaster preparedness and response at local, subnational, and National levels.
5. Capacity building on Core Humanitarian Standards:
The Core Humanitarian Standards Training Manual contributed to improving the knowledge and efficiencies of the local humanitarian actors (NDRNet, municipality, and provincial authorities). This enabled them to promote and enhance their essence and understanding of disaster risk reduction and management to a wider audience.

Engagement with NDRRMA through

Department of Science and Technology (DoST) have not issued adequate guidelines on inter-agency coordination.
This meant that the implementation of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Plan (NDRRMP) has not been well-coordinated and the accountability of the agencies has not been well-defined.
“Hence, the country’s DRRM is wanting of clear policy guidelines for a well-coordinated disaster prevention and mitigation efforts,” the report read.
The report said that despite their vital roles, the DoST and the Office of Civil Defense have not reviewed and monitored the Mines and Geosciences Bureau’s planning of the updates on the Geo-Hazard Mapping and Assessment Project (GhMAP).
DoST and OCD serve vital functions as vice-chairperson for disaster prevention and mitigation and lead agency for enhanced community-based monitoring, respectively.
But, the CoA said they have only supervised the projects they implement, and have not coordinated and reviewed the updating of the GhMAP.
No budget for monitoring
The CoA also observed that the OCD had inadequately monitored the program, which meant there was no assurance that the effectiveness of the program had been consistently evaluated.
The OCD is responsible for ensuring the implementation of the NDRRMP, and the integration of local governments’ DRRM plans in their development and land use plans.
But, the CoA found that the OCD was unable to validate the agencies’ accomplishment reports because, from 2013 to 2015, Congress did not at all provide it with the capital outlay to purchase the necessary equipment. OCD also turned out to be understaffed, as only 59 percent of its 644 positions were filled up.
Well-utilized
Still, the CoA found that generally, local government units were able to utilize the geo-hazard maps in formulating their local disaster preparedness and comprehensive land use plans.
It cited a survey of 79 local government units in Central Luzon, Calabarzon, and Western Visayas. Seventy-six of them (96 percent) have taken the maps into account for their planning activities, although only 45 of the LGUs (60 percent) used the latest maps provided by MGB.
Even then, the disaster risk assessment helped “contribute to the reduction of vulnerabilities and exposure of communities in case of disasters,” the report noted.
It highlighted Antipolo City, site of the deadly Cherry Hills Subdivision landslide in 1999, as well as Pasig City as examples of cities that have integrated the disaster
